subject: giant trevally
title: This Fish Tracks Flying Birds From Below, Then Leaps and Grabs Them

scenes.text: Fishermen swore a fish was eating birds in mid-air. Nobody had a single photo.
It's the giant trevally. It can weigh 176 pounds, and usually hunts alone.
But every year, over half a million terns nest on one Seychelles atoll, and the trevally gather.
When fledglings take their first flights over the lagoon, the fish watch from below, track one and match its speed.
Then they launch out of the water and take it in mid-air.
The BBC finally filmed it for Blue Planet Two. The fishermen were right.

description:
A fish that catches flying birds in mid-air sounded like a fisherman's tale until it was filmed.
Giant trevally, which can reach 80 kg (176 lb) and usually hunt alone, gather at Farquhar Atoll in the Seychelles when more than half a million sooty terns nest there. As the fledglings learn to fly low over the lagoon, the fish watch from underwater, track a bird, match its speed and launch themselves out of the water to seize it. The BBC's Blue Planet II team followed up a rumour from South African fishermen and filmed the behaviour for the first time; director Miles Barton said there had not been a single picture or video clip of it.
Did you know a fish could do this? Comment below.
first_comment: The BBC director called the shoot their biggest gamble: not one photo of it existed. Which predator should we cover next?
